newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Bund vol slips as rate rise talk recedes.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Bund vol slips as rate rise talk recedes.

text.p: Implied volatility of Bund options traded on LIFFE slid on Tuesday after the Bundesbank quelled expectations that a rise in German interest rates was imminent, traders said.
Speculation that interest rates would rise had been mounting in recent weeks, after dollar/mark scaled a near eight-year high over 1.89 marks in early August.

But earlier the German central bank set a tender for 14-day securities repurchase agreements at an unchanged fixed rate of three percent, signalling that monetary policy remains unchanged for now. Also July M3 data showed growth at 5.7 percent, within the central bank's corridor.
"With growth well within the target range, a rate rise is less likely," said a trader at a U.S. bank. "The market tone has changed today."

Traders said comments late on Monday by Bundesbank council member Hans-Juergen Krupp, which suggested a rise in interest rates would be damaging to the domestic economy, had also helped dampen speculation of a rate hike. The Bundesbank council meets on Thursday.

October Bund options on December futures were at an implied volatility of 5.25 percent by 1030 GMT, down from 5.4 percent at the open. December options were at 5.3 percent, also down from 5.4 percent.
September options, which expire on Thursday, were at 6.5 percent. A broker at a major British brokerage said there was a flurry of last-minute punts going through in September.
September futures were up 0.24 at 102.70, while December was up 0.27 at 101.88.
The broker said locals were sellers of volatility, and he expected it to slide towards 5.2 percent once the Bundesbank council meeting on Thursday was out of the way.
Volume of trade was moderate, traders said. Notable trades include 500 lots of the 99.50/98.00 December put spread bought by a French house.
